Prothom Alo (10 Feb 2024), citing a BMET source: 8 of 20 smart cards whose applications had been rejected on the 'Ami Probashi' app and then cleared, the subject of a BMET inquiry, were taken in the agency's name on 2 and 3 Jan 2024; the inquiry committee held no one responsible and said hackers may have used an additional director general's login; the agency could not be reached (RL as printed by the source); OEP status Active (28 Oct 2026 list)

Prothom Alo (10 Feb 2024), citing a BMET source: 12 of 20 smart cards whose applications had been rejected on the 'Ami Probashi' app and then cleared, the subject of a BMET inquiry, were taken in the agency's name on 1 and 3 Jan 2024; the inquiry committee held no one responsible; MD Shamim Mahmud Patwary says it applied and got clearance as usual and knows of no irregularity (RL as printed by the source); OEP status Active (28 Oct 2026 list)

Prothom Alo (8 Mar 2025): the agency's owner Md Rafiqul Islam is a co-accused in the case a Satkhira woman filed in a Satkhira court on 16 Feb 2025, saying she was sent to Saudi Arabia for a cleaner's job, given domestic work and sexually abused; he told Prothom Alo she came back in January because she was already ill and could not work (named as 'M/s Siam Trade International' of Dhaka; RL matched by name to OEP list entry 'M/S. SIAM TRADE INTERNATIONAL', Paltan, Dhaka); OEP status Active (28 Oct 2026 list)

Prothom Alo (29 Oct 2024): a father filed a case on 28 Oct 2024 at the Barishal Human Trafficking Offences Tribunal, which ordered police to record it, against the MD of SJ Group, a recruiting agency in Purana Paltan, Dhaka, and two others; the case alleges they took Tk 4.5 lakh each (Tk 1.035 crore) from 23 young men for jobs at a Saudi solar-panel company at SR 1,800 a month, but after arrival on 4 May 2024 they worked 45 days on a Hajj project for SR 615; 12 were caught as irregular migrants and deported and 11 are untraced (a case, not a verdict; no OEP entry under this name)

Prothom Alo (29 Oct 2024): a father filed a case on 27 Oct 2024 at the Barishal Human Trafficking Offences Tribunal against an official of M R International (Chairmanbari, Dhaka) and two others; the case alleges they took Tk 3.8 lakh to send his son to Saudi Arabia on 15 May 2024, where he got no job and was handed to a trafficking ring that tortured him and demanded Tk 5 lakh under threat of death (a case, not a verdict; no OEP entry under this name)

Prothom Alo (22 Sep 2025): the Bangladesh embassy in Abu Dhabi said false reports of a UAE visa ban on Bangladeshis came from an article on uaevisaonline.com, a so-called visa processing centre; the embassy says the Dubai head-office address the website gives does not exist and most customer reviews it holds allege customers were financially cheated

Prothom Alo (10 Sep 2026): returnee Rajon Hossain says 30 Bangladeshis flew to Russia on 7 May 2026 through the agency, promised electrician jobs, with visas, BMET cards and police clearance; there they signed a contract in Russian that turned out to be an army contract, were trained and sent to the front on 12 Jun, and 17 were killed on 14 Jun; a relative of the dead worker Al Mamun alleges the fraud was done through the agency, which promised Tk 1.5 lakh a month, and his family says sending him cost about Tk 8.5 lakh (named as 'Jabal-E-Noor International Limited'; RL matched by name to OEP list entry 'JABAL-E-NOOR INTERNATIONAL LTD.', whose licence the Ministry cancelled on 1 Jun 2026 over the same 30 workers who left on 7 May (C0008, C0009)); OEP status Cancelled (28 Oct 2026 list)

Prothom Alo (29 Jun 2026): four families' written complaint to the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare on 19 May 2026 says a recruiting agency in Malibagh, Dhaka, took Tk 7 lakh each (Tk 28 lakh) and their papers to send four Gopalganj men to Russia, and that they left on 7 May with BMET clearance; the families say the men were handed to the army and told them each had been sold to Russian forces through the agency for Tk 30.75 lakh; a father says the agency gave no help and threatened them (named as 'Jabel-e-Noor International Limited' of Malibagh; RL matched by name to OEP list entry 'JABAL-E-NOOR INTERNATIONAL LTD.', whose licence the Ministry cancelled on 1 Jun 2026 over the same 30 workers who left on 7 May (C0008, C0009); OEP gives its address as Purana Paltan); OEP status Cancelled (28 Oct 2026 list)

Prothom Alo (21 Oct 2026): the SRB (Special Response Battalion) said at a 14 Oct 2026 press conference that 30 Bangladeshis went to Russia on 7 May through Jabale Noor, RS International and TS Group, each charged about Tk 10 lakh on average for promised construction jobs, and on arrival had their passports and phones taken and were handed to the Russian army; Jabale Noor International's founder Mizanur Rahman and Abu Taher alias Lentu, called ringleaders of the trafficking ring, were arrested on 13 Oct (an arrest, not a verdict; named as 'Jabale Noor'; RL matched by name to OEP list entry 'JABAL-E-NOOR INTERNATIONAL LTD.', whose licence the Ministry cancelled on 1 Jun 2026 over the same 30 workers who left on 7 May (C0008, C0009); Prothom Alo says the Ministry cancelled Jabale Noor's licence over the 30 workers; families' letters place it in Khilkhet, OEP in Purana Paltan); OEP status Cancelled (28 Oct 2026 list)

Prothom Alo (21 Oct 2026): 28 letters families submitted to the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare in July 2026 say their relatives went to Russia through brokers, that Jabale Noor International of Khilkhet and RS International of Ashulia sent them, and that, lured by high pay, they were sold to the Russian army and readied for war (named as 'Jabale Noor International'; RL matched by name to OEP list entry 'JABAL-E-NOOR INTERNATIONAL LTD.', whose licence the Ministry cancelled on 1 Jun 2026 over the same 30 workers who left on 7 May (C0008, C0009); OEP gives its address as Purana Paltan, not Khilkhet); OEP status Cancelled (28 Oct 2026 list)

Prothom Alo (21 Oct 2026): the Bangladesh embassy labour wing in Moscow wrote to the Ministry on 25 May 2026 that RS International was at first told it could bring 10 workers but this was suspended when suspicion arose, and that on 18 May a worker's family told the embassy 30 men had come to Russia through Jabale Noor and RS International and were being sent to the war front (RL matched by name to OEP list entry 'M/S RS INTERNATIONAL'); OEP status Cancelled (28 Oct 2026 list)

Prothom Alo (21 Oct 2026): the SRB said at a 14 Oct 2026 press conference that 30 Bangladeshis went to Russia on 7 May through Jabale Noor, RS International and TS Group, each charged about Tk 10 lakh on average for promised construction jobs, and were handed to the Russian army instead (RL matched by name to OEP list entry 'M/S RS INTERNATIONAL'; families' letters place it in Ashulia, as OEP does); OEP status Cancelled (28 Oct 2026 list)

Prothom Alo (11 Jun 2026): families allege RS International, a recruiting agency, sold four Patgram (Lalmonirhat) youths to a Russian mercenary force after promising garment-factory and IT jobs; they say local men took Tk 9 lakh from each and the agency sent them to Moscow via Bahrain on 8 May 2026, where their passports, visas and phones were taken; on 7 Jun its Dhaka office in Sector 15, Uttara, was found locked (RL matched by name to OEP list entry 'M/S RS INTERNATIONAL', whose licence address is Ashulia; the article calls the Uttara office its Dhaka office); OEP status Cancelled (28 Oct 2026 list) RL not assigned: the four left on 8 May separately from the 30 whose case led to RL1428's cancellation, and the article places the agency's office in Uttara while RL1428's licence address is in Ashulia; unconfirmed name match.

Prothom Alo (21 Oct 2026): the SRB said 30 Bangladeshis went to Russia on 7 May 2026 through Jabale Noor, RS International and 'TS Group', each charged about Tk 10 lakh for promised construction jobs, and were handed to the Russian army; Prothom Alo identifies the third agency as TS Overseas and found it took BMET clearances for 266 workers to Russia over four years, while the other two names were not in BMET's database (named as 'TS Group' by the SRB; RL matched by Prothom Alo's identification to OEP list entry 'T S OVERSEAS LTD'); OEP status Cancelled (28 Oct 2026 list)

Al Riffat International', Suspended, with no address)

summary: Prothom Alo (15 Jul 2025): the CID arrested chairman Khairul Bashar in Dhanmondi on 14 Jul 2025 in the money-laundering case it filed at Gulshan police station on 4 May 2025, which alleges he, his wife and son took Tk 18 crore from 141 students promised higher study abroad; a CID officer told the court 448 victims have come forward; the plaintiff's lawyer showed the court photos of people beaten by Bashar's men when they went to the office for refunds; Bashar told the court he is 'a victim of circumstances' (an arrest, not a verdict)

agency: BSB Global Network (study-abroad consultancy; no RL)
summary: Prothom Alo (15 Jul 2025): cases by at least 100 people have been filed against chairman Khairul Bashar at Gulshan police station and courts across the country from Oct 2024 to 30 Jun 2025, with arrest warrants issued; they include a case for 18 people filed on 5 May 2025 by a lawyer couple who say they paid Tk 34 lakh for Canadian student visas that never came, and a case by 23 people filed on 28 Dec 2024 alleging Tk 1.8 crore taken (cases, not verdicts)

agency: BSB Global Network (study-abroad consultancy; no RL)

agency: BSB Global Network (study-abroad consultancy; no RL)
summary: Prothom Alo (6 and 13 Aug 2025): a Dhaka court remanded chairman Khairul Bashar for three days on 6 Aug 2025 in a further case alleging he embezzled Tk 1.18 crore promising higher study abroad, and for 13 days on 13 Aug in five separate fraud cases brought by Gulshan police; the CID says many students' applications were never filed with any foreign university

Prothom Alo (1 Mar 2025): Tareq Aziz of Cumilla told a press conference that former Chhatra Shibir leader Ashek Elahi took him and his family to Tourism Aid Limited, an agency in Farmgate, Dhaka, where a Tk 45 lakh deal was made to send him to the US via Nepal, Brazil and the Mexican border; he says he was held in Kathmandu from Dec 2023 and forced at gunpoint to tell his father he was in Mexico, after which his father paid Tk 43 lakh; Ashek Elahi denies it and says he too was a victim (no OEP entry under this name)

Prothom Alo (5 Aug 2026): police arrested Nabil Yusuf at East Rajabazar, Farmgate, on 4 Aug 2026 in a case filed at Uttara East police station on 12 Jul by Zarin Tasnim, which alleges about Tk 3.105 crore was taken from at least 36 people through a firm named VisaGuide on promises of student visas abroad; cheques and receipts were given but no one was sent or refunded, and by 5 Jul the office had moved; four other accused have been arrested (an arrest, not a verdict)

agency: Arzu Immigration Limited (unlicensed per SRB; no RL)

Prothom Alo (15 Feb 2025): police and families say Rashed Khan of Shariatpur, who runs a firm called Lamisa Enterprise and sends people abroad, gathered people from Shariatpur and Madaripur through associates; 24 who set out for Italy through Libya have had no contact with their families since 21-22 Mar 2024; families have filed 11 cases against him and his associates, and the CID arrested him in Jatrabari, Dhaka, on 14 Feb 2025 (an arrest, not a verdict; no OEP entry under this name)

agency: Euro Visa Help Center BD, Natore (visa office; no RL)

S. Alam Overseas' RL0754 is a Purana Paltan licence, Cancelled, valid until 31 Dec 2013)

summary: Prothom Alo (20 Nov 2026): victims of S Alam Overseas' Azerbaijan scam allege the medical centre colluded with the firm, which made all who handed in passports take their medical test there for Tk 5,000 each; the centre's MD Md Jasimuddin denies any collusion and says the firm had 70-80 tests done there at Tk 2,500 each and still owes the centre about Tk 1.5 lakh

Prothom Alo reports families of 18 young men from Sadar upazila, Shariatpur, say Rashed Khan of Char Jadabpur, who runs a firm called Lamisa Enterprise and sends people abroad through two associates, took Tk 12-20 lakh each in 2022-23 to send them to Italy irregularly via the UAE, Egypt and Libya; some were jailed or held for ransom in Libya, none has been heard from since 21-22 Mar 2024, Rashed has locked his village house and his Paltan, Dhaka office is shut; the families held a human chain and gave the Deputy Commissioner a memorandum, and the police superintendent said a shadow investigation would start (no case filed yet; no OEP entry under this name)
